chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about a man who performs wudu (ablution) and then touches the inner part of his anus. He said:

“He has invalidated his wudu (ablution). And if he touches the inner part of his urethra, then he must repeat the wudu (ablution). And if he is in the salat (prayer), he cuts off the salat (prayer), performs wudu (ablution), and repeats the salat (prayer). And if he opens his urethra, he repeats the wudu (ablution) and repeats the salat (prayer).”

key_terms.بَاطِنَ إِحْلِيلِهِ: the inner part of his urethra
key_terms.بَاطِنَ دُبُرِهِ: the inner part of his anus

ai.seo_question: Does touching the inner private parts invalidate wudu (ablution) and require repeating salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on acts considered to invalidate wudu (ablution). It states that touching the inner part of the anus or the inner part of the urethra necessitates renewing wudu (ablution), and if this occurs during salat (prayer), the prayer must be stopped and repeated after purification.
